predictions.experiment: First-marker regrade of the base's wrong T1 answers: among T1 rows graded wrong by grader v3 on the full text, the fraction whose first answer marker is right.
predictions.recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl (500 rows, base + cue, T 1.0). For each row, v3_last = grader/rln4_grader_v3.py applied to the full text against gold (recomputed, since the record has no v3 column). First marker = whichever of these starts earliest in text: (a) a line whose left-stripped text begins with 'Answer:', with content = the rest of that line; (b) the first '\boxed{', with content = the brace-balanced contents. first_score = grader v3 applied to the string 'Answer: ' + content against gold. A row with no marker gets first_score 0. Filter: rows with v3_last == 0, cap hits included. Statistic: (rows with first_score == 1) / (rows with v3_last == 0).
predictions.not_computable: grader v3 (rln4_lib.grade_v3 -> n13_score.grade) needs the math_verify package, which this python3 does not have; the standard library cannot reproduce grader v3's equivalence test
predictions.note: File: s3://pg-lineage-769063704696/results/rlneurons/r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl -> runs/theory-tests/s3/T1.jsonl (500 rows, one per problem). v3_last = rln4_lib.grade_v3(gold, text), the function grader/rln4_grader_v3.py calls; text includes the 3-token cue ' line!\n\nOkay'. First marker: the earliest of (a) the first line whose left-stripped text starts with 'Answer:' (case-sensitive; '**Answer:**', 'Final Answer:' and mid-line 'Answer:' do not count) and (b) the first '\boxed{'. first_score = grade_v3(gold, 'Answer: ' + content). Edge cases: an empty 'Answer:' line is still the first marker and scores 0; an unbalanced first '\boxed{' (only possible near the end of a capped text) scores 0; box content with a newline is graded only up to that newline because v3 reads a marker's rest of line. ALT reading: first marker = the earliest candidate under grader v3's own candidate set (MARK_V3 anywhere in a line with a non-empty rest, which includes 'Final Answer:', 'Answer is' and mid-line 'Answer:', or the first balanced box), graded the same way. At least one stored row (problem 54) ends '...0.15.Answer: 0.15' in the middle of a line, so the two readings can differ. RISK: grader v3's equivalence needs math_verify (plus numpy, which is stubbed if missing because it is only used in annotations). This laptop's python3 has no math_verify, so in this environment the script prints not_computable.

predictions.experiment: Direction of first/last disagreement on T1: among rows where the first-marker grade differs from the last-marker grade, the share that are first-right and last-wrong.
predictions.recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl, all 500 rows, cap hits included. v3_last and first_score are defined exactly as in the previous recipe (first marker = earliest 'Answer:' line or '\boxed{'; no marker gives first_score 0). Discordant rows: first_score != v3_last. Statistic: (discordant rows with first_score == 1) / (discordant rows). If there are no discordant rows, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: measured below 0.45, or no discordant rows

predictions.note: Same file, first-marker definition and grading as p1; all 500 rows, cap hits included. Discordant rows: first_score != v3_last. Main = discordant rows with first_score 1 / discordant rows; no discordant rows prints refuted with measured null. ALT = the same ratio with p1's alternative first marker (grader v3's own candidate set). Rows with no marker have first_score 0, so a row with no line-start 'Answer:' and no box that v3 grades right (e.g. through a mid-line 'Answer:' or 'Final Answer:') counts as discordant first-wrong/last-right. That pushes the main number down, and the ALT reading removes most of it. Needs math_verify, as in p1.

predictions.note: File: iterate-runs:abaybektursun-1114-183640-e828/answers.jsonl, fetched to runs/theory-tests/day1_3/<job>/answers.jsonl. Before the run it held 2,041 rows: 2,000 attempt-0, 32 attempt-1 and 9 attempt-2. Same computation as p3; refuted_by = measured > 0.004. RL's prompt asks for an 'Answer:' line. If RL writes a box early, for example in a mid-solution check, and its final answer on a later 'Answer:' line, the first marker is that early box, which can make the net negative. If RL writes only a mid-line 'Answer:' or a '**Answer:**' line, the main reading finds no marker and gives 0, which also makes the net negative. Neither case can push the number above 0.004 unless first-marker answers are right where the last one is wrong. ALT = v3-candidate first marker. Needs math_verify.

predictions.experiment: Wrong rate among base answers that keep going and state a new answer after the first one: among finished T1 answers with more than 300 characters and at least one further marker after the first marker, the fraction graded wrong by v3.
predictions.recipe: File: s3 r4/base_rl-02/out/T1.jsonl. Filter: cap_hit false and at least one marker (first marker defined as in the first recipe). End of first marker: for an 'Answer:' line, the end of that line (or the end of text); for '\boxed{', the position just after its matching closing brace. Keep rows where the text after that end is longer than 300 characters AND contains another 'Answer:' line (a left-stripped line beginning 'Answer:') or another '\boxed{'. Statistic: (kept rows with v3_last == 0) / (kept rows), with v3_last recomputed by grader/rln4_grader_v3.py. If no rows are kept, the statistic is undefined and counts as refuted.
predictions.refuted_by: measured below 0.20, or no kept rows

predictions.note: File: T1.jsonl as in p1. Filter: cap_hit is False and a first marker exists (p1's definition). End of the first marker: for an 'Answer:' line, the position of its newline (or the end of text); for a box, just after the matching brace (the end of text if unbalanced). Kept: text[end:] longer than 300 characters (the newline after an 'Answer:' line counts as one of them) AND (a line that starts at or after end and whose left-stripped text begins with 'Answer:', or '\boxed{' anywhere in text[end:]). Statistic = kept rows with recomputed grade_v3 == 0 / kept rows; no kept rows prints refuted. ALT reading, from the experiment text's 'answers with more than 300 characters': the whole answer longer than 300 characters instead of the text after the first marker, with the same further-marker condition. Caveat: a common base layout 'Answer: X' followed by '\boxed{X}' is kept only when more than 300 characters follow the first marker, so benign restatements can be counted too. Needs math_verify.
